rows.note: CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T08:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small eruption seen centered at approx. N40E05 beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T08:15Z as seen in SDO AIA 193. Dimming signatures extending to the Southeast (approx. N20E25) seen in SDO AIA 193 and proximity to a small coronal hole indicate a potential strong SE deflection of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Updated measurement based on source location and later frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T13:38Z, as well as to the North in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME is likely far sided, and can be seen as field line opening from beyond the West limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T13:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely far-sided and may not be observed, with the only potential observation in GOES SUVI 284 starting ~2026-10-21T20:14Z as field line movement on/near the N limb; however faint high northern latitude on-disk brightening near this time in GOES SUVI 284 indicates that motion may trace on-disk and not to the far-side. In STEREO A EUVI 195/304, a change in field lines and prominence material can be seen on the west limb after a lengthy data gap ends spanning approximately 2026-10-21T15:15Z to 2026-10-21T20:45Z, and may indicate the source without directly observing the eruption. Based on the current estimated location of former Active Regions 14545 and 14549 around E150-E170 and the triangulated analysis, those former regions may be the source for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Shock triangulation with SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The shock front is notably difficult to observe in COR2 imagery, and the width from LASCO and CCOR-1 is best used for the fit. As such, the parameters may vary slightly.
Preliminary bulk triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, but a good fit of the brightest material and may be final analysis.

rows.note: Thin CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 with a data gap starting at 2026-10-22T17:23Z. The source is likely far-sided, only potentially visible as faint field line motion over the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-22T19:18Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky with the unobserved likely far-sided source and no available STEREO A COR2 imagery to triangulate.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a real time data gap spanning 2026-10-22T17:53Z to 2026-10-23T01:23Z, where it may be too faint to observe afterwards. No distinct source is observed on disk and may be far-sided, with weak field line movement over the NE limb as early as 2026-10-22T20:00Z in SDO AIA 171 noted as a potential, weak candidate.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only plane-of-sky due to the unobserved source and lack of available STEREO A COR2 observations for triangulation.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C1.3 flare and eruption from Active Region 14557 (centered near N10W90) starting around 2026-10-23T03:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Despite data availability during this time, this event is likely far-sided from the perspective of STEREO A and is therefore not observed by STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

rows.note: A super faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source seen in EUV imagery, so this outflow is possibly far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky analysis with SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 and no source for it has been found in EUV imagery.

rows.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-24T15:12Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely related to field line movement seen beyond the NE in in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-10-24T14:42Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: A very minor CME to the E only seen in GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph; the CME is covered by the unfilled scheduled data gap in SOHO LASCO coronagraph. No source has been seen in EUV imagery for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in GOES CCOR-1 and is not seen in STEREO A COR2. It is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO. No source for it has been found. Only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

rows.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap from approximately 2026-10-24T16:48Z - 2026-10-24T20:36Z. No source is observed in available EUV imagery, including STEREO A EUVI, and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only plane-of-sky.

rows.note: A narrow jet-like CME seen to the WSW in all three coronagraphs. No source has been found for this jet-like feature in the EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the narrow front of this jet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and the STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and not confirmed by source location, as no source has been found in the EUV imagery.

rows.note: Relatively narrow CME to the NNW seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3 because of poor image quality. It is covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2 so far. The source is likely the opening/movement of field lines and possibly small ejecta seen on/beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171/131/304 after 2026-10-24T21:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in GOES CCOR-1 but not seen in C3 because of poor image quality; it is covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely the opening/movement of field lines and possibly small ejecta seen on/beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171/131/304 after 2026-10-24T21:12Z. Only plane-of-sky analysis is possible so far.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided, observed in GOES SUVI 284 as field line movement beyond the W limb around 2026-10-24T22:06Z, and may be directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 as brightening in the vicinity of former AR 14551 at 2026-10-24T20:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting STEREO misses most of the CME and there is difficulty tracking the front only at the edge of its field-of-view.

rows.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source is wide field line movement over the E limb starting around 2026-10-25T02:09Z in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304; the prominence on the limb jostles in SDO AIA 304/GOES SUVI 304  but does not cleanly erupt. Preceeded by and overtakes a faint leading edge starting at 2026-10-25T01:48Z measuring ~173 km/s, from field line movement over the NE limb ~2026-10-25T00:58Z in GOES SUVI 284 prior to the main eruption. Followed by and overlaps with a streamer blowout starting around 2026-10-25T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This analysis includes the fainter northern lobe of the front in SOHO LASCO C2/C3; with no separate source indication and traveling together they are analyzed as one. Front is harder to observe in STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, starting very slow. It is either not yet seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-10-25T10:09Z or too faint to resolve the leading edge. The source appears to be a mix of continued slow field line movement over the E limb following CME 2026-10-25T03:12Z, whose eruption began around 2026-10-25T02:09Z in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304, and/or further field line movement in GOES SUVI 171/284 starting around 2026-10-25T04:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky. One COR2A frame before the data gap may see the faint front, but is not reliable enough to confirm a 3D longitude with so far.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. It is likely not observed in STEREO A COR2, but the NW quadrant of COR2 imagery is overlapped with prior CME activity and may obscure this front. The source is likely far-sided, due to the lack of any on-disk EUV observations corresponding to this front time.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky due to the uncertain, likely far-sided, source and no visiblity in STEREO A COR2 for triangulation.

rows.note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-25T19:24Z. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen in SDO AIA 304 located at approx. S10W60, beginning at approx. 2026-10-25T18:42Z. Field line opening is also seen in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely far-sided over the east limb, potentially observed as field line movement in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-25T23:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap. The source may be related to an opening of field lines visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2026-10-25T23:55Z, likely associated with a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this CME. The source may be related to a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75) seen best in SDO AIA 131/193/304 imagery starting around 2026-10-26T01:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

rows.note: CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME precedes and is partially overlapped by the larger CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this leading edge and CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z. For this leading edge, the eruptive source is likely field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193, and on-disk brightening in SDO AIA 304 and STEREO A EUVI 304, starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z and centered around S09W72. This eruption is also associated with a C1.9 flare peaking at 2026-10-26T08:38Z, observed in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Despite the source location around S09W72, the fit does not work unless it is around W40-W50, so we may be observing significant deflection not seen well in corresponding EUV imagery.

rows.note: CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME follows the more faint CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this front and CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z. For this CME, the eruptive source is likely an area of dimming and field line movement centered ~S05W80 in the vicinity of AR 14561, observed in SDO AIA 171/195, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304, starting around 2026-10-26T09:10Z. This follows separate field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z ~S09W72, likely responsible for preceding CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Despite the source location around S05W80, the fit does not work unless it is around W45-W50, so we may be observing significant deflection not seen well in corresponding EUV imagery.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery despite data availability, likely because it is directed towards the spacecraft and therefore occulted by the coronagraph. The source is related to an eruption and C2.8 flare from Active Region 14561 (S12W77) starting around 2026-10-26T18:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.  This event was also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 after a downlink data gap backfilled and was seen in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-10-26T20:38Z to 2026-10-27T02:23Z. The source is a large filament eruption visible near the eastern limb which begins to lift off around 2026-10-26T20:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 imagery. The filament may extend as far as longitude E50 to beyond the east limb. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

rows.note: Narrow CME visible to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and the NE in STEREO A COR2. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement on/near the high latitude N limb around 2026-10-27T22:31Z in SDO AIA 171, or far-sided and unobserved.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C2, and STEREO A COR2.

The source is likely former AR 14561, located around S10W95 at this time. There is no distinct, clean eruption associated with this CME, but rather slow field line movement and brightening from this region of the disk in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-10-28T09:46Z, also observed as some field line movement and brightening near AR 14561 in STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only 3D analysis using the estimated source observation ~S10W95 as a basis. As such, the parameters may vary slightly. The front is barely visible in STEREO A COR2 white light imagery but not reliably resolvable in its running difference imagery for triangulation.

The source is a filament eruption with liftoff starting around 2026-10-29T07:36Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The footpoints extend from about S20W20 to S10W50. Post eruptive dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 with an opening of field lines seen over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: Very minor and faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. Its source is a very minor eruption from the former AR 14561 (S10W130) starting ~2026-10-30T11:25Z as seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. AR 14561 rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-10-27.

cmeAnalyses.note: An approximate analysis based on the location of the (very minor) source and the imagery in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 coronagraphs and not confirmed by triangulation since the front is not seen in STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-31T05:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2, as it may be obscured by the pylon or too faint to view clearly. The source of this event is an eruption from former AR 14561 (S11W140) beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T04:30Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195. Brightening near the region and dimming extending Northward can be seen in association with this eruption, possibly suggesting a Northern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: Diffuse CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T00:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen centered at approx. S15E65 beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T23:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171/193. This eruption is in close proximity to a coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: CME first seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T19:00Z. The CME is also visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may be faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen centered at approx. N15W15. Filament destabilization began at approx. 2026-11-01T16:43Z, with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T17:54Z as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement are also visible in SDO AIA 193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and one frame usable frame of STEREO A COR2, noting poor quality COR2 imagery affecting front visibility beyond one frame into a real-time data gap starting 2026-11-01T19:38Z.

rows.note: Slow developing CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2, also observed in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR due to a data gap in real-time starting at 2026-11-01T19:38Z. The source of this event is an eruption from beyond the NE limb seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T18:14Z as filament ejecta and very wide, slow field line movement. An initial faint CME at 2026-11-01T18:36Z (LASCO C2) measuring plane-of-sky ~164 km/s is observed prior to this brighter emerging front.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only plane-of-sky with no STEREO A COR2 available to triangulate the far-sided source. This front starts very slow and speeds up, altering its shape slightly with a faster nose emerging in later frames; this behavior aligns with the GOES SUVI observed erupting field line activity.
Updated measurement with later frames of STEREO A COR2 to provide a 3D longitude fit.
